title: k8s-bootstrap-orchestration-checklist-ipxe-and-vsphere-notes
summary: Working checklist and Terraform module notes for orchestrating on-prem k8s bootstrap across bare-metal (iPXE/ignition) and vSphere templates. Focus: repeatable idempotent bootstrap, small control-plane HA pattern, rollback/upgrade plan for kubeadm upgrades, and hints for module interfaces.
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures a pragmatic orchestration checklist and module-level notes for our on-prem k8s bootstrap flow. It is intentionally informal — think of it as a runbook for an engineer who needs to stand up a cluster quickly and repeatably across two common environments: bare-metal using iPXE + ignition (or cloud-init) and vSphere templated VMs.

Scope and assumptions:
- Target k8s versions: 1.26 -> 1.27 upgrades tested here.
- Control-plane: 3 nodes for HA (kubeadm stacked etcd).
- CNI: Calico (BGP mode for bare-metal); on vSphere we prefer IP-in-IP because BGP is often unavailable.
- Load balancer: MetalLB for bare-metal; vSphere uses NSX/HAProxy LB or native LB depending on customer.
- Authentication: dex + OIDC integrated after bootstrap (out-of-scope for initial join).
- Images and templates are pre-built and reachable from local registry or vSphere datastore.

High-level flow (both environments):
1) Provision infrastructure (PXE DHCP options / vSphere VMs) via Terraform modules.
2) Ensure network prerequisites: VLANs, routing for pod networks, MTU checks, kube-proxy mode decision.
3) Bootstrap first control-plane node (kubeadm init with --upload-certs).
4) Join control-plane nodes using the control-plane join token / certs.
5) Deploy CNI, CoreDNS, CSI drivers.
6) Validate cluster health and register worker nodes.
7) Snapshot / export cluster bootstrap artifacts for future diagnostics (kubeadm-config, etcd snapshots).

Checklist: pre-provisioning (Terraform modules)
- Inventory inputs: node hostnames, IP addresses (or DHCP), BMC credentials for bare-metal.
- Module interface suggestions:
  - module compute: (count, cpu, mem, disk_gb, image_id, host_profile)
  - module network: (vlan_ids, mtu, pod_cidr, service_cidr, dns_servers)
  - module provisioning: (ipxe_base_url, ignition_bucket, tftp_server)
  - outputs: provisioned_nodes (list of {name, ip, mac, bmc})
- Idempotency: Terraform modules must not destroy bootstrap data on reapply (mark metadata with tags or an out-of-band state file).
- Secrets: store kubeadm join tokens in sealed-secret or HashiCorp Vault — do not put them in TF state.

Bare-metal provisioning notes (iPXE + ignition):
- Boot flow recommended: iPXE -> initramfs -> cloud-init/ignition download -> kubelet configured via system unit.
- Use machine-init images that take a metadata URL param. Keep initramfs small and readable.
- DHCP config: add option 67 to chainload iPXE; provide PXE menu by MAC prefix for rescue vs bootstrap.
- ignition vs cloud-init: preference = ignition for atomic, reproducible OS config (if using CoreOS/RHCOS). Use cloud-init for Ubuntu-based flows.
- matchbox vs netboot.xyz: matchbox gives better control for production but needs its own HA story.
- BMC power cycle plan: include a pre-provision step to verify IPMI/Redfish reachability and to set boot-order to PXE.

vSphere provisioning notes (templates + guest customization):
- Use OVF/template with cloud-init enabled. Keep template with minimal extra packages (kubelet, crictl optional).
- Use vCenter guest customization to set hostname and network; avoid ephemeral customization that breaks idempotency — prefer metadata-drive approach (OVF env).
- Storage: VMFS vs vSAN considerations; prefer thick-provisioned OS disks for predictable performance.
- Datastore sizing: collect PVC patterns early — control-plane etcd needs fast IO.
- Template tagging: tag templates with image_version and k8s_compatibility metadata to enable future upgrades.

kubeadm specifics and config snippets (conceptual):
- kubeadm-config.yaml should be generated from template with explicit apiServer.certSANs and advertiseAddress.
- Use featureGates where required (e.g., TTLAfterFinished for cleanup jobs).
- Recommend: apiVersion: kubeadm.k8s.io/v1beta3 (verify based on target version).
- Enable --upload-certs once and then rotate via k8s Job after cluster is stable for security hygiene.

Upgrade plan (control-plane first):
- Preflight: run upgrade-checks (kubeadm upgrade plan), verify CRDs and in-tree deps.
- Take etcd snapshot from primary control-plane and copy snapshot off-host.
- Upgrade sequence:
  1) Drain and cordon kube-system non-critical pods (but keep etcd stack).
  2) Upgrade kubeadm on first control-plane, run kubeadm upgrade apply <version>.
  3) Upgrade kubelet & kubectl and restart kubelet, verify Node Ready.
  4) Repeat for remaining control-plane nodes.
  5) Upgrade control-plane static pods (if using static pod manifests).
  6) Upgrade worker nodes (drain, upgrade kubelet, uncordon).
- Rollback: if a control-plane node fails to rejoin or etcd is unhealthy, restore etcd from snapshot to a quarantine cluster or to the original nodes (documented restore steps).

Testing & validation checklist:
- Verify etcd member list and health (etcdctl endpoint status).
- kubeadm token validity and cluster-info mapping.
- End-to-end pod scheduling, DNS resolution, and CNI connectivity across nodes.
- Load balancer health checks hitting all control-plane nodes.
- Latency test for control-plane API (p95 under SLA).

Terraform module notes and patterns:
- Keep provisioning modules small — one responsibility per module (compute, network, provisioning).
- Provide a separate "bootstrap-data" resource module that writes ignition artifacts to object storage (minio / s3) and returns signed URLs.
- Avoid embedding large files in TF state; use external data sources to fetch heavy artifacts.
- Use null_resource with triggers for out-of-band actions (e.g., call Ansible or a small bootstrap worker to set BMC).
- Example outputs the cluster operator wants: cluster_bootstrap_time, first_cp_ip, ignition_url, provision_log_url.

Common gotchas we've seen in previous runs:
- MTU mismatch between host NIC and VxLAN encapsulated pod networks causing dropped packets. Always run an MTU probe script pre-bootstrap.
- Image pull failures in air-gapped envs due to missing registry mirrors — build a mirror plan and test pull-through caches.
- Kubeadm join token expiry: for long-running provisioning windows, prefer pre-created CSRs or certificate-based joins.
- Race on CNI deployment: delaying CNI until all control-planes present can avoid split-brain pod networking.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide default behavior for kube-proxy mode (ipvs vs iptables) on bare-metal with Calico BGP.
- Should Terraform create the MetalLB configmap (address pools) or leave that to post-bootstrap operator?
- Explore using kind of ephemeral bootstrap cluster (nested VMs) for safe upgrade rehearsals.

Quick commands (notes, not copy/paste production):
- kubeadm init --config kubeadm-config.yaml --upload-certs
- kubeadm join <api-server>:6443 --token <token> --discovery-token-ca-cert-hash sha256:<hash> --control-plane --certificate-key <key>
- etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-snap.db --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/apiserver-etcd-client.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/apiserver-etcd-client.key

Notes for oncall and runbooks:
- If control-plane is unreachable, verify LB config and BGP neighborship (bare-metal).
- Keep a minimal rescue image on USB for bare-metal with tools: ipmiutil, dhcpdump, ethtool, and a static kubeconfig to query etcd health.

Appendix: short end-to-end example for a single control-plane bootstrap (summary):
- Provision VM / bare-metal node with IP 10.10.0.10.
- Ensure BMC reachable and bootorder set to PXE (if bare-metal).
- Boot first node, run kubeadm init with advertiseAddress 10.10.0.10 and podCIDR 10.244.0.0/16.
- Install Calico manifest tailored to environment (BGP vs IP-in-IP).
- Record kubeadm join control-plane command output to secure store.
- Join second and third control-plane nodes using the recorded join command.

If you are iterating on this doc: leave short notes inline and tag the next owner. This is intentionally terse — expand specific vendor steps (Dell/HP iDRAC, HPE iLO, vSphere customization spec snippets) into separate child docs when we standardize.
